flow_ref: User story (not in any OCMS flow deck)
code_summary: ocmsadminapi crud/ocmsizdb/stagemap (StageMap, StageMapController, StageValidationService), crud/ocmsizdb/parameter (Parameter, ParameterController), crud/ocmsizdb/OcmsChangeOfProcessing/ChangeOfProcessingService, workflows/notice_creation/core/helpers/NoticeProcessingHelper. ocmsadminprivateapi framework/workflows/agencies/toppan/upload (ToppanStage, ToppanUploadHelper, ToppanLettersGeneratorJob), framework/schedulers/ToppanUploadJobsScheduler, agencies/lta/download/helpers/LtaProcessingStageManager. ocmsadminui pages/System (ParameterList, ParameterForm), App.tsx. ocmseserviceapi, ocmseserviceui, thirdpartyapi: no stage-configuration code
note: The story asks that an officer can configure the processing stages (pre-notice to warrant) per notice type. The sheet status 'Fully paid' is not fully supported by the code. The stage order that actually moves notices is read by the Toppan cron from table ocms_stage_map (with a fallback to the ToppanStage enum); the same table is also used by furnish validation. There are five problems. (1) ocms_stage_map has read endpoints only (/stagemaplist and /plus-get-stage-map) and no UI page, so changing the order means changing the database. (2) The generic Parameter page can save NEXT_STAGE_<stage> rows, but those rows move no stage: the only reader that decides a stage (the automatic branch of updateVonStage in ChangeOfProcessingService) is never called because both callers (portal CPS and PLUS) use manual mode, and the rest only orders the notice list. (3) There is no per-notice-type configuration: the ocms_stage_map key is the stage only, the ocms_parameter key is parameter_id + code only; behaviour per notice type/vehicle type is hardcoded (NoticeProcessingHelper, offence type U rule in ChangeOfProcessingService). (4) The Toppan loop always runs over the fixed ToppanStage enum (RD1..DR3, ANL) and the executeJob() call in the day-end scheduler is commented out, so letter generation runs only through the manual trigger. (5) A manual stage change by the officer sets the next stage to the chosen stage and the date to now, not from configuration. Pre-notice (NPA/ROV/ENA) and court/warrant stages are not part of this configurable loop. Real parameter values on the server: cannot verify from repo; no ocms_parameter seed SQL was found in the repo.
recommendation: Claim only very little. What can be shown: the Toppan cron reads the stage order from table ocms_stage_map. Still missing: a UI/API to change it, per-notice-type configuration, and NEXT_STAGE_* parameters that are really used. Ask URA/the team to confirm whether changing it through the database is accepted for this story, or mark it as a gap

steps.step: The processing stage order (pre-notice to warrant) is read from database configuration, not hardcoded
steps.detail: The Toppan cron reads the next stage from ocms_stage_map (getNextProcessingStageFromMap, ToppanUploadHelper.java:140-148). If no row exists it falls back to the ToppanStage enum (RD1>RD2>RR3>DN1>DN2>DR3, ToppanStage.java:19-25) and RR3/DR3 fall back to 'CPC' (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1814-1823). Parameter NEXT_STAGE_<stage> in ocms_parameter is read only in the automatic branch of updateVonStage (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1120-1127), which is never called because both callers use manual mode (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1035, 1498), and for the sort order of the notice list (OcmsValidOffenceNoticeServiceImpl.java:585-605 in ocmsadminprivateapi). So the only source that really moves stages is ocms_stage_map plus the enum fallback. Some transitions are still hardcoded, for example the LTA cron moving ROV to ENA with next stage RD1 (LtaProcessingStageManager.java:432-434). The real row values on the server: cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: The officer changes the next stage from the staff portal
steps.detail: There is no write endpoint for ocms_stage_map: StageMapController only has POST /stagemaplist (StageMapController.java:42-49) and /plus-get-stage-map is also read-only (StageMapControllerPlus.java:39-45). There is no stage map page in ocmsadminui (grep stagemap/stage_map in ocmsadminui/src is empty). What the officer can edit is only ocms_parameter rows (Parameter ID NEXT_STAGE_<stage>, Code NEXT_STAGE) through System > Parameter (App.tsx:375-396; the patch accepts only description and value, ParameterController.java:98-118). Those rows are not used to move stages: the reader in CPS is never called (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1035, 1498) and the Toppan cron uses ocms_stage_map, so editing them changes the stage order nowhere except the sort of the notice list. The value is only required, with no check that it is a valid stage (ValidParameter.ts:44-46). Function OCMS_SYSTEM_PARAMETER is mapped in api-authorization.properties:166-167; which roles hold it: cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: Stage configuration can differ for each notice type
steps.detail: ocms_stage_map is keyed only by last_processing_stage + next_processing_stage (StageMap.java:20-28) and ocms_parameter by parameter_id + code (Parameter.java:28-38). Neither has a notice type column. Per-notice-type behaviour exists but is hardcoded: notice type O with vehicle type V/S/D starts at ROV (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:924-928), vehicle type X starts at DN1 (NoticeProcessingHelper.java:949-953), and CPS returns success without any change for offence type U to DN1/DN2/DR3/CPC (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1312-1316). Changing them needs a code change and deployment.

steps.step: The cron moves notices between stages automatically following the configured order
steps.detail: Per stage, resolveStageContext takes the next stage from ocms_stage_map and the number of days from STAGEDAYS (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1810-1830), and next_processing_date is computed from it (ToppanUploadHelper.java:1368-1370), so the DB data is used. But the loop always runs over ToppanStage.values() (RD1, RD2, RR3, DN1, DN2, DR3, ANL; ToppanLettersGeneratorJob.java:151-156), so a new stage added through data would not be processed. The call toppanLettersGeneratorService.executeJob() in executeDayEndJobs is commented out (ToppanUploadJobsScheduler.java:118); letters run only through the manual trigger POST /toppan/generate-letters (ToppanUnifiedController.java:34), so 'the cron advances stages daily' is at most Sebagian. In prod sftp.upload.disabledServers=toppan (application-prod.properties:86), so the delivery gate is bypassed and the stage still advances without delivery (OCMS-DF-2026-192, Ready to UAT). The real server value: cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: When the officer changes the stage manually, the next stage follows the configured order
steps.detail: The portal CPS and the PLUS path both call updateVonStage(von, stage, true) (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1035, 1498). In manual mode next_processing_stage is set to the stage chosen by the officer and next_processing_date to the current time (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1093-1118; the comment cites the OCMS15 specification). The branch that reads NEXT_STAGE_<stage> (ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1120-1127) is only reached through the overload updateVonStage(von, stage), which has no caller, so it never runs. The parameter validation at ChangeOfProcessingService.java:1323-1351 only writes warnings. The configured order is not used when the stage is changed manually.
